title: Explain Common Networking Ports, Protocols, Services, and Traffic Types

sections.title: What You Are Learning
paragraphs: Network services use protocols and ports so systems know what service is requested, where traffic belongs, and how communication should behave. This objective also covers IP protocol types, IPSec components, and traffic-delivery patterns.
bullets: ICMP, TCP, UDP, GRE, and IPSec
sections.callout: Service → protocol → port → transport or network behavior → traffic type.

sections.title: Maestro Focus
paragraphs: When CompTIA supplies a port number, protocol, service, security function, or delivery pattern, can you identify its role immediately?

entries.title: FTP - 20/21
paragraphs: FTP transfers files but does not inherently protect credentials or content.

entries.title: SFTP and SSH - 22
paragraphs: SSH provides encrypted remote shell access. SFTP uses SSH functionality for secure file transfer.

entries.title: Telnet - 23
paragraphs: Telnet provides an unencrypted remote terminal and should not be confused with SSH.

entries.title: TFTP - 69
paragraphs: TFTP is a simple file-transfer protocol with fewer capabilities and security features than robust alternatives.

entries.title: RDP - 3389
paragraphs: RDP provides graphical remote access to Windows systems.

entries.title: DNS - 53
paragraphs: DNS resolves names and other DNS records.
entries.recognitionCue: A host name must resolve to an address → DNS 53.

entries.title: DHCP - 67/68
paragraphs: DHCP automatically supplies IP addressing, subnet mask, gateway, DNS, and other client configuration.
entries.recognitionCue: A client must obtain an address automatically → DHCP 67/68.

entries.title: NTP - 123
paragraphs: NTP synchronizes time, which supports accurate logs, authentication, troubleshooting, and security.
entries.recognitionCue: Network devices have inconsistent clocks → NTP 123.

entries.title: SNMP - 161/162
paragraphs: SNMP supports monitoring and management. Port 161 is associated with queries and management; 162 with traps and notifications.
entries.recognitionCue: A device sends an unsolicited monitoring notification → SNMP trap 162.

entries.title: Syslog - 514
paragraphs: Syslog carries event and log messages to a centralized collector.
entries.recognitionCue: Network devices forward logs centrally → Syslog 514.

sections.title: Web, Mail, Directory, Database, and Voice Services

entries.title: HTTP 80 and HTTPS 443
paragraphs: HTTP provides web communication on 80. HTTPS protects web communication on 443.

entries.title: SMTP 25 and SMTPS 587
paragraphs: SMTP transfers email on 25. For this objective, associate secure mail submission or transfer with SMTPS on 587.

entries.title: LDAP 389 and LDAPS 636
paragraphs: LDAP accesses directory services on 389. LDAPS protects LDAP communication with SSL/TLS on 636.

entries.title: SMB - 445
paragraphs: SMB provides network file, folder, printer, and other resource sharing.

entries.title: SQL Server - 1433
paragraphs: Microsoft SQL Server commonly listens on 1433.

entries.title: SIP - 5060/5061
paragraphs: SIP establishes and manages voice and video communication sessions.

entries.title: Internet Control Message Protocol (ICMP)
paragraphs: ICMP carries IP control and diagnostic messages, including echo request and reply used by ping. ICMP does not use TCP or UDP port numbers.

entries.title: Transmission Control Protocol (TCP)
paragraphs: TCP is connection-oriented and uses sequencing, acknowledgments, and retransmission to provide reliable delivery.

entries.title: User Datagram Protocol (UDP)
paragraphs: UDP is connectionless, has less overhead, and does not provide TCP-style delivery guarantees.

entries.title: Generic Routing Encapsulation (GRE)
paragraphs: GRE encapsulates one network protocol inside another for tunneling. GRE alone does not provide encryption.

entries.title: Internet Protocol Security (IPSec)
paragraphs: IPSec is a suite used to protect IP communications through authentication, integrity, confidentiality, and security-association negotiation.

entries.title: Authentication Header (AH)
paragraphs: AH provides authentication and integrity protection but not payload confidentiality through encryption.

entries.title: Encapsulating Security Payload (ESP)
paragraphs: ESP can provide payload confidentiality through encryption and can also support integrity and authentication.

entries.title: Internet Key Exchange (IKE)
paragraphs: IKE negotiates security parameters, security associations, and keys used by IPSec peers.

entries.title: Unicast
paragraphs: Unicast is one sender to one specific receiver.

entries.title: Multicast
paragraphs: Multicast sends from one source to a selected group of receivers that participate in the group.

entries.title: Anycast
paragraphs: Anycast sends traffic to one member of a group, commonly the nearest or best instance according to routing.

entries.title: Broadcast
paragraphs: Broadcast sends from one source to all members of the local broadcast domain and is especially associated with IPv4 LAN behavior.

sections.title: Recognition Cues
bullets: Encapsulation tunnel without inherent encryption → GRE

entries.title: SSH/SFTP vs. Telnet
paragraphs: SSH and SFTP use 22 and are secure. Telnet uses 23 and is unencrypted.

entries.title: ICMP vs. TCP/UDP
paragraphs: ICMP is its own IP protocol and does not have a TCP or UDP port.

entries.title: GRE vs. IPSec
paragraphs: GRE provides encapsulation. IPSec provides security. GRE alone does not imply encryption.

entries.title: AH vs. ESP vs. IKE
paragraphs: AH authenticates and protects integrity; ESP provides confidentiality; IKE negotiates keys and associations.

entries.title: Anycast vs. Multicast
paragraphs: Anycast reaches one member of many possible destinations. Multicast reaches the selected group.

sections.title: Maestro Recognition Sheet

Unicast one; multicast group; anycast one of many; broadcast all local
